study_identification_part.si_4_title: Revealing Individual Neuroanatomical Heterogeneity in Alzheimer Disease Using Neuroanatomical Normative Modeling

dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.detail: The study uses two main data sources: (1) a reference data set (n=33,072) compiled from multiple publicly available sources including OASIS, ABCD, and UK Biobank among others detailed in eTable 1 (Kia et al.), acquired across 60 sites; (2) a clinical target data set from ADNI (n=1,492) acquired across 62 sites. The reference data set composition is described in detail in Kia et al. (ref 27) and summarized in eTable 1 (not available in this paper). OASIS, ABCD, and UK Biobank are explicitly named; additional datasets in the reference set are unspecified in this paper. MULTI-DATASET is assigned because the reference data set combines 9 or more data sets across 60 sites.
dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.supporting_text: "The reference data set was made by combining data on healthy people from multiple publicly available sources, including OASIS, Adolescent Brain Cognitive Development study, and UKB, detailed in eTable 1" ... "The clinical data used in the preparation of this article were obtained from the ADNI database." ... "In the reference data set, a total of n = 33,072 T1-weighted MRI scans were collated across 60 sites (this sample is described in detail in Kia et al. and summarized in eTable 1)"
dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.location: Verdi2023.pdf.md: Methods / Participants, L80-L82; Results / Participants, L150

answer.MULTI-DATASET (UNSPECIFIED OR N\u003e\u0: reference/training data for normative model (n=33,072 across 60 sites from 9 data sets including OASIS, ABCD, UK Biobank, and others)

answer.ADNI: clinical target data set; 70% of ADNI healthy controls (n~462) used for transfer learning calibration to adapt normative model to ADNI sites; remaining 30% of controls (n=159) + MCI (n=662) + AD (n=206) used for clinical assessment of heterogeneity

dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.detail: The normative model was trained on the large reference data set (n=33,072) using hierarchical Bayesian regression. The model parameters were then recalibrated (transfer learning) to ADNI using 70% of healthy controls per ADNI site. The remaining 30% of healthy controls plus MCI and AD participants formed the final clinical evaluation set (n=1,027).
dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.supporting_text: "A hierarchical Bayesian regression model was trained on multisite data to generate normative models per region using the covariates age and sex. This was based on the population variation in the reference data set (training data)" ... "the parameters of the reference normative model were recalibrated to the ADNI data set using 70% of healthy controls per ADNI site" ... "The remaining 30% of healthy controls plus MCI and patients with AD were used to assess the heterogeneity in neuroanatomical presentation."

model-1.model-name: hierarchical Bayesian regression normative model for cortical thickness

dc_3_number_of_healthy_control_of_each_n.detail: There is one normative model in this study. The reference data set (n=33,072) was used to train the normative model. In addition, 70% of ADNI healthy controls (~462 from total ADNI controls of 621) were used for transfer learning calibration (site adaptation), but these are not additional training data for the normative model itself. The paper does not report a separate train/test split within the 33,072 reference data set, so the overall-phase and train-phase are both reported as 33,072. The final clinical evaluation used 159 healthy controls (30% of 621 ADNI controls) alongside MCI and AD participants.
dc_3_number_of_healthy_control_of_each_n.supporting_text: "In the reference data set, a total of n = 33,072 T1-weighted MRI scans were collated across 60 sites" ... "Here, by training on over n = 33,000 from only 9 data sets (with 60 sites), the model produces a stable distribution of estimates across the entire lifespan."
dc_3_number_of_healthy_control_of_each_n.location: Verdi2023.pdf.md: Results / Participants, L150; Methods / Neuroanatomical Normative Modeling, L99

dc_4_age_info_of_each_normative_nodel.detail: The age information for the reference data set (n=33,072) used to build the normative model is not directly reported in this paper. The paper states the reference data set is 'described in detail in Kia et al. (ref 27) and summarized in eTable 1', but eTable 1 is a supplementary material not included here. The paper mentions the model covers 'the entire lifespan', and the reference dataset includes sources such as ABCD (developmental ages), OASIS, and UK Biobank (older adults), suggesting a wide age range. The ADNI clinical data set demographics are reported (mean 72.3 +/- 7.4, range 56.1-92.5) but these are clinical target participants, not the normative model training sample.

dc_5_sex_info_of_each_normative_nodel.detail: The sex information for the reference data set (n=33,072) used to build the normative model is not directly reported in this paper. The reference data set demographics are described in Kia et al. (ref 27) and eTable 1 (supplementary material not available here). The ADNI clinical data set sex breakdown is reported in Table 1 (total 728 male : 764 female out of 1,492) but these are clinical target participants, not the normative model training sample.
